firstFailure.rootCause: The r09 fixture made a descendant hold the wrapper's channels via stdio 'inherit'+IPC. On Windows, libuv stdio pipe handles are not inheritable by grandchildren through any tested spawn form ('inherit', integer fd, or classic handle inheritance), so the direct child's exit closed the channels and the wrapper correctly returned COMPLETED inside the deadline. Empirically, the deeper mechanism is that each Node spawn on Windows creates a kill-on-close job object: when the direct child exits (voluntarily or terminated), the job closes and the operating system hard-terminates all of its descendants, including mid-boot ones.

platformInvestigation.method: Instrumented synthetic processes (heartbeat files, pid probes, full process-event logging) under the local evidence root repro-inherit/; never killed or enumerated by image name; diagnostics read-only
windowsFacts: 'inherit', integer-fd, and all-ignore stdio cannot hand a wrapper pipe write end to a grandchild: the wrapper sees EOF within milliseconds of the direct child's exit

the direct child's libuv kill-on-close job object terminates every descendant at that child's exit, within hundreds of milliseconds, whether the child exits voluntarily or is terminated; descendants dying mid-boot never run their first line
therefore 'descendant outlives the direct child' and 'normal completion with a still-running descendant' are not constructible on Windows
an already-exited PID is not signalled again by the wrapper; bounded return still reports descendantState=NOT_VERIFIED because the wrapper observes neither the job termination nor any survivor
platformInvestigation.posixFacts: Untestable on this Windows host this round; the POSIX branches keep the r09 semantics (fd-sharing pipe holder, surviving descendant) and are exercised by repository CI/Linux runs

The deadline case keeps the full r09 assertion set on POSIX (forcedPipeClosure=true with a live pipe holder) and asserts the Windows-constructible state (child alive holding its own channels at deadline, CANCELLED/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, directChildExitObserved, descendant untouched by the wrapper, NOT_VERIFIED).
